subtitle: An independent review of how the website performs for a first-time, full-fee patient — what it does well, and where attention is lost before a booking is made.
summary: The writing on this first screen is genuinely good. “Top Med Spa in Plano TX for Natural-Looking Results” names the town and the promise in one line, and the two paragraphs beneath it name the treatments — Botox, dermal fillers, advanced skin treatments, laser, medical weight loss — and add “medically guided”. “Enhance your natural beauty—not change it” speaks directly to the fear that stops most first-time injectable patients. The photograph is the practice's own reception, chandelier and all, rather than a stock interior.

The problem is a single design decision. Two buttons sit beneath that copy: “Book Your Consultation” drawn as a thin outline, and “Explore All Treatments” filled in solid black. The eye goes to the solid one every time — so the most visually dominant action on the page is the one that leads to more browsing, while the one that earns money is the quieter of the two. The header carries a strong “Book Now”, but on a phone that disappears into the menu and the inverted pair is all that remains.

Evidence limitation: this review covers the homepage on desktop and mobile plus publicly visible information. Treatment-page depth and technical performance were not assessed, so the score is normalised across the six categories that were. Nothing here uses private analytics, and no traffic or revenue figures have been estimated.
scoreNote: Normalised across six assessed categories (90 points available). The positioning and local signals score close to full marks. Most of what is lost sits in two categories — proof, and which button is drawn to look important.

scorecard.finding: Town, promise and treatments all named before the scroll.
No rating, review count or named clinician on the first screen.
Book Now in the header, but the hero pair is the wrong way round.
The browse button is styled more strongly than the booking button.
Calm and readable; Book Now and the phone are both in the menu.
Plano, TX named twice on the first screen.

strengthsLead: The hard part — knowing what to say and saying it plainly — is already done here.

strengths.title: The headline names the town and the promise together.
strengths.body: “Top Med Spa in Plano TX for Natural-Looking Results.” Proximity and outcome in one line, which is the pair of questions a patient answers first. A great many practices manage neither.

strengths.title: “Enhance your natural beauty—not change it.”
strengths.body: This is the single best sentence on the page. The fear that stops a first-time injectable patient is looking overdone, and this addresses it directly rather than talking around it.

strengths.title: The treatments are named in the opening copy.
strengths.body: Botox, dermal fillers, advanced skin treatments, laser services and medical weight loss, plus “medically guided”. Someone searching for any one of those can self-qualify without clicking anything.

strengths.title: The photograph is the actual reception.
strengths.body: Their own front desk and chandelier, not a stock interior. A patient can recognise the room when they arrive, and premises photography quietly proves the practice is real in a way a purchased image never does.

strengths.title: Financing is offered before it is asked for.
strengths.body: “Buy Now, Pay Later through Affirm & Klarna” in the bar above, and Financing carried in the main navigation. Removing the affordability objection early converts patients who would otherwise never enquire.

captionDesktop: Desktop, 1366×768. The headline names Plano and the promise. Beneath it “Explore All Treatments” is filled solid while “Book Your Consultation” is a thin outline.
captionMobile: Mobile, 390×844. Calm and readable, but Book Now and the telephone number have both moved into the menu.

findings.heading: The browse button is drawn more strongly than the booking button.
findings.evidence: In the hero, “Book Your Consultation” is a thin black outline on white. Directly beneath it, “Explore All Treatments” is a solid black block with white bold text.
findings.why: Visual weight tells a visitor which action the business prefers. Here the heavier of the two leads to more reading, and the lighter one is the appointment. A patient who was ready to book is invited to browse instead — and browsing is where hesitation returns.
findings.recommended: Swap the two styles. “Book Your Consultation” takes the solid fill and sits first; “Explore All Treatments” becomes the outline beneath it. No new work, no new copy — the same two buttons the other way round.

findings.heading: Nothing on the first screen is independently verifiable.
findings.evidence: No rating, review count, award or named clinician appears on the opening screen. The claim “Top Med Spa in Plano TX” is stated by the practice about itself, and “medically guided” does not say by whom.
findings.why: Everything a visitor reads here is the practice's own account. For a medical treatment at this price the decisive question is who performs it and what other patients say, and neither is answered before the visitor is asked to book. “Top med spa” is also the phrase every competitor uses, so it does not distinguish.
findings.recommended: Put the Google rating with its review count beside the booking button, and name the supervising clinician with a photograph and qualification. That converts “medically guided” from a phrase into a person.

findings.heading: Booking and the telephone number both move into the menu.
findings.evidence: At 390×844 the header carries the logo and a menu button only. The “Book Now” button present on desktop is not shown, and no telephone number appears on the first screen.
findings.why: The strong header booking button is the one element that survives everywhere on desktop, and on a phone it is the first thing to go — leaving the inverted button pair as the only visible action. The patient who would rather telephone has nothing at all to tap.
findings.recommended: Keep a compact Book Now in the mobile header alongside the menu button, and add a tap-to-call icon beside it.

findings.heading: The consent panel takes the lower quarter of the screen.
findings.evidence: On both desktop and mobile a cookie notice occupies the foot of the first screen, with Accept all and Manage cookies. On mobile it begins immediately beneath the second button.
findings.why: Less severe here than on many sites, because the buttons remain visible above it. It is still the last thing in the visitor's eye-line at the moment they are deciding, and it competes with the action the page wants.
findings.recommended: Reduce it to a slim bar. The choices can stay exactly as they are.

psychology.plain: People expect a site to behave like the others they use.
psychology.site: Conventional and calm. Nothing here asks the visitor to learn anything unfamiliar.

psychology.plain: Important actions should be big and easy to thumb.
psychology.site: Both hero buttons are generous targets on a phone. The header booking button is absent there.

psychology.plain: Reassurance has to sit where the doubt is.
psychology.site: No rating, review or credential sits anywhere near either button.
“Medically guided” is stated but nobody is named, so the authority has no face attached to it.
Two steps are offered and the visually stronger one is the one that does not earn.

psychology.plain: Sensible pre-selections that serve the patient.
psychology.site: Naming the treatments in the opening paragraph, and offering financing before it is asked for, are both genuinely helpful.

psychology.plain: Balanced, realistic communication is trusted more than perfection.
psychology.site: “Enhance your natural beauty—not change it” is credible and well judged. “Top Med Spa” is the one line that is not.

roadmap.actions: Swap the two hero button styles so booking is the solid one. Add a Book Now and a tap-to-call to the mobile header. Reduce the consent panel to a slim bar.
Add the Google rating and review count beside the booking button. Name the supervising clinician with a photograph and qualification. Replace “Top Med Spa” with something checkable.

Treatment-page depth with candidacy and downtime notes, particularly for injectables and weight loss. Post-treatment review requests. Begin measuring enquiry-to-booking so the calculator figures above become yours.

limitations: This review assessed the homepage at 1366×768 and at 390 pixels wide, together with publicly visible information. Treatment-page depth and technical performance were not assessed and are excluded from the score rather than estimated; the total is normalised across the six categories reviewed (90 points available). The consent panel behaves differently for returning visitors who have already answered it.
